question: A 25-year-old woman presents with a high-grade fever of 101.1°F (38.4°C) and complaints of dysuria. She has a previous history of spontaneous vaginal delivery 4 days ago. Her labor was uneventful and she was discharged on 2nd day after her delivery. On per abdominal examination, her uterus is well contracted at 18 weeks-size. On vaginal examination, normal-looking lochia is seen and an intact episiotomy scar is noted. Breast examination is normal. Which of the following is the first step in her management?

answers.option: Admit her and start intravenous antibiotics and antipyretics
Pelvic ultrasound for retained products of conception
Send urine detailed report and culture and CBC

question: A 30-year-old woman para 2 delivered vaginally an hour ago. She then developed postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony. All medical treatment was provided but the patient is currently still bleeding. Vitals are also now unstable. Which of the following is the most appropriate surgical method to treat the patient?

A 36-year-old gravida 2 para 1+0 lady is advised by her doctor for a 1st-trimester serum biochemical screening test for Down's syndrome. Which of the following screening tests is done in the 1st trimester?

answers.option: Pregnancy associated plasma protein and alpha fetoprotein
Pregnancy associated plasma protein and βhCG

question: A 20-year-old primigravida presents to the antenatal clinic. She is 16 weeks pregnant and is a known case of sickle cell disease. Which of the following will be the main step in her antenatal management to prevent sickle cell crisis?

A 20-year-old primigravida lady came to the labor ward at the 37th week of gestation with complaints of a gush of fluid and regular, painful uterine contraction. After 2 hours, a Caesarian section was performed due to non-progress of labor with the same findings. The baby weighed 3kg (6.6 lb). Which one of the following is the most likely cause of her non-progress of labor?

A 20-year-old primigravida lady is currently 32 weeks pregnant and her ultrasound shows a small-for-gestational-age fetus. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation for this patient?

A 20-year-old primigravida woman presents in the emergency department at 30 weeks of gestation with complaints of breathlessness and fatigue. On examination, her pulse is 130 beats per minute and her blood pressure is 110/60 mmHg. She is a diagnosed case of mitral stenosis and is at stage II NYHA classification. Which of these will be the aim of her treatment?

A 24-year-old gravida 4 para 3 woman presented to the antenatal clinic at 32 weeks of gestation with complaints of severe abdominal distention. In her previous pregnancy, the labor was difficult and the weight of the baby was 4 kg (8.8 lb). Symphysis-fundal height (SFH) is 38 cm and her abdomen is tense. Her mother is diabetic. Which of the following is the most likely cause of increased symphysis-fundal height?

A 22-year-old gravida 3 para 1+0 woman was admitted to the emergency department with mild vaginal bleeding at 35 weeks of gestation. She also complained of moderate abdominal pain since 4 hours and had a stony, hard abdomen. She was previously diagnosed with hypertension and her blood pressure was 130/90 mmHg and pulse was 120 beats per minutes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 22-year-old gravida 5 para 3+1 lady comes to the antenatal clinic at 28 weeks of gestation. She complains of lightheadedness and fatigue. She is habitual of tobacco for 6 years. Blood examination shows Hb 7.9 gm/dl and MCV 76 fl and MCH 20 pg/l. Which of the following is the best prescription for her problem?

A 22-year-old primigravida came to the clinic at 22 weeks of gestation. She is a known case of diabetes for 2 years and is currently on insulin injections. How will she be advised for glycemic control with blood sugar levels during her pregnancy?

answers.option: Preprandial 3.5-4.5 mmol/l and 2 hours postprandial 4-6.5 mmol/l
Preprandial 2.5-4.5 mmol/l and 2 hours postprandial 4-6.0 mmol/l
Preprandial 3.5-5.5 mmol/l and 2 hours postprandial 4-6.5 mmol/l
Preprandial 3.5-4.5 mmol/l and 2 hours postprandial 4-6.0 mmol/l
Preprandial 3.5-5.5 mmol/l and 2 hours postprandial 4-6.0 mmol/l

question: A 22-year-old female gravida 3 para 2+0 came to the labor room at 40 weeks of gestation with complaints of strong labor pains for an hour. All her previous deliveries were spontaneous vaginal deliveries. On per abdominal examination, symphysial fundal height was 39 cm. Uterine contractions were 3/10 (45-50 sec) while the fetal heart was 140-150 beats per minute. On vaginal examination, the cervix was 5 cm dilated, presenting part was cephalic, the vertex was high, and the cervix was 70% effaced and central. Soon after the examination, she had a spontaneous rupture of membranes at the next uterine contraction. Fetal bradycardia of 70-80 beats per minute was noted. Which of the following will be the next step in her management?

answers.option: Perform fetal scalp sampling to exclude fetal acidosis
Give oxygen, place in left lateral position and prepare for Caesarean delivery
Perform assisted vaginal delivery with forceps
Perform vaginal examination to exclude cord prolapse
Start syntocinon infusion to expedite the delivery

question: A 24-year-old gravida 1 para 0 woman had induction of labor due to gestational hypertension at 39 weeks gestation. She needed a lower section cesarean section due to non-progress of labor. The baby was delivered without difficulty through a low-transverse incision. Upon delivery of the placenta, profuse bleeding was noted from the uterus, reaching around 1500 mL. Which of the following will be the first step in the management while senior help is being summoned?

A 24-year-old primigravida presented to the labor room with complaints of labor pain. She is 39 weeks pregnant and on vaginal examination, cervical dilation is 3 cm. She requested adequate pain relief for labor. Which of the following is most effective in pain relief in labor?
A 24-year-old primigravida at 29 weeks of gestation is admitted for preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM). Which of the following is the recommended antibiotic for PPROM?

A 25-year-old P1+0 came to the clinic for her antenatal checkup. Her last child was born 2 years ago by normal vaginal delivery. Her hemoglobin was 10.9 g/dl at 32 weeks of gestation. How will she be classified according to her anemia status?

A 25-year-old para 1+0 lady was found to have a fever of 100°F (37.8°C). She previously underwent an emergency lower segment cesarean section 18 hours ago, under general anesthesia due to fetal distress. On examination, her respiratory rate was 22 breaths per minute. She had a cough and on auscultation, a chest wheeze was noted. On per abdominal examination, the uterus was 18 weeks size and the dressing was dry and intact. Which of the following could be the most likely cause of her fever?

A 25-year-old patient presented in the emergency department with complaints of fever, pain, erythema and swelling of the left breast. She gave a history of delivery 3 weeks ago. After examination, a diagnosis of breast abscess was made. Which of the following is the most commonest organism involved in this pathology?

A 28-year-old gravida 3 para 2 woman came for antenatal booking in the 24th week of her pregnancy. She has a history of preterm births in both previous pregnancies. Which of the following does she require?

A 25-year-old primigravida came to the clinic at 34 weeks of gestation with a complaint of high blood pressure for 1 month. On examination, blood pressure is 140/95 mmHg, edema ++, symphysis fundal height is 32 cm and fetal heart rate is 142 beats per minute. Which of the following is an appropriate initial test to check for fetal growth?

A 25-year-old primigravida came to the emergency department at 41 weeks of gestation. She was sure that she remembered her last menstrual period accurately and was then planned for induction of labor. Which of the following is the most common reason for induction of labor?

A 25-year-old primigravida was fully dilated and on per vaginal examination, the vertex was seen in occipito-posterior (OP) position. Which of the following is the most common cause of persistent OP position?

A 25-year-old primigravida came to the emergency department in her second trimester with complaints of severe chest pain and dyspnea. She has previously been diagnosed with sickle cell disease. Her hemoglobin was 7.5 g/dl. Which of the following will be done as immediate management?

A 25-year-old primigravida lady who was 6 weeks pregnant visited the antenatal clinic. She was prescribed folic acid 0.4 mg daily. Which of the following will these folic acid supplements help prevent?

A 26-year-old para 3+0 gave a history of all her previous pregnancies as pre-term vaginal births at 32, 30, and 30 weeks of gestation. She was diagnosed as having a bicornuate uterus on a hysterosalpingogram. All her neonates had developed respiratory distress syndrome and needed ventilatory support. She had two alive issues and one of the children had developed complications of prematurity. Which of the following maternal treatments is associated with improved neonatal outcomes in preterm babies?

A 26-year-old woman gravida 3 para 0+2 comes to the clinic in the 13th week of gestation. She was previously diagnosed with hypothyroidism 2 weeks ago. She is currently on thyroxine 50 μg 2 tablets daily.  Which of the following will help her maintain biochemical euthyroidism?

A 26-year-old primigravida lady comes to the OPD at 28 weeks of her gestation for a routine antenatal visit. She has a family history of diabetes and hypertension. Currently, she has no active complaints. On examination, her blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg and her pulse is 84 beats per minute. Symphysiofundal height (SFH) is 28 weeks and fetal heart rate is 142 beats per minute. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation for her at this gestational age?

A 26-year-old obese lady, gravida 3 para 2+0, comes to the clinic at 20 weeks of gestation. She had a family history of diabetes and a previous history of delivering good-sized (macrosomic) babies. Which of the following is an appropriate screening test for gestational diabetes at this stage of her pregnancy?

A 26-year-old para 2+0 woman comes to the clinic with complaints of dyspnea while doing routine work. She was previously diagnosed with Mitral stenosis and is currently 34 weeks pregnant. What will she be classified as according to the New York heart association (NYHA) classification of heart failure?

A 26-year-old primigravida lady at 36 weeks of her gestation presented to the clinic with an ultrasound report showing fetal abdominal circumference as >97th centile. An oral glucose test was performed which indicated gestational diabetes. What would be an appropriate immediate management plan for her?

A 28-year-old gravida 3 para 2+0 lady presented to the clinic at 36 weeks of gestation with complaints of loss of fetal movements for 2 days. On examination, her blood pressure was 120/80 mmHg, her pulse was 80 beats per minute and she was afebrile. On per abdominal examination, symphysis fundal height was 36 cm, and fetal presentation was cephalic with 4/5 engagement. Fetal heart sounds were absent. On vaginal examination, the cervical os was closed and the cervix was not effaced. Which of the following will be the most appropriate method for induction of labor in this patient?

A 28-year-old, gravida 3, para 2+0, female is brought to the emergency department in a state of unconsciousness for a day. Her attendant gives a history of fever and vomiting for the past week. Currently, her GCS is 9/15, she is jaundiced with a blood pressure of 90/60 mmHg and a temperature of 100°F (37.8°C). On abdominal examination, symphysis fundal height is 30 cm, presentation is breach, and fetal heart sounds are present. Her liver function test shows SGPT 5,200 IU/L, total bilirubin as 18 mg/dl, direct bilirubin as 16.4 mg/dl, and platelet count as 152, 000 mcL. Which of the following is the most likely virus causing her condition?

A 28-year-old primigravida woman comes to the clinic and is diagnosed with preeclampsia with mild to moderate intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR). Which one of the following tests is required serially for the best assessment of fetal well-being?

A 28-year-old gravida 2, para 1+0 presented to the obstetrics clinic in her 24th gestational week. She had a history of eclampsia in her previous pregnancy and was worried about developing similar complications during her current pregnancy. Which of the following will be the best method of predicting any possible complication?

A 30-year-old para 2 lady delivered a 4 kg (8.8 lb) baby boy after forceps application. She suffered from a 3rd-degree perineal tear. Which of the following do 3rd-degree perineal tears normally involve?

A 30-year-old gravida 2 para 1+0 woman was admitted to the labor room at 38 weeks of gestation with labor pains. Initially, her labor was progressing at a rate of 1 cm/hr but after reaching 7 cm dilation, her progress was arrested despite adequate uterine contractions. Which of the following could be the most probable cause of her arrest?

A 30-year-old gravida 3 lady came to the antenatal clinic at 42 weeks of gestation. All her previous deliveries for spontaneous vaginal deliveries. Which of the following complications can her baby develop?

A 30-year-old gravida 2 lady came to the clinic for a routine antenatal checkup during her 32nd gestational week. Her CBC showed a platelet count of 100 x 10⁹/L. Which one of the following is a common cause of thrombocytopenia in pregnancy?

A 30-year-old lady comes to the clinic with a history of gestational amenorrhea for 18 weeks. This is her second pregnancy. On ultrasound, she is seen to have dichorionic, diamniotic gestational sacs. How frequently will she be offered antenatal visits?

answers.option: Total 9 visits including screening of diabetes and hypertension
She should be called for antenatal visit fortnightly throughout her pregnancy
Total 6-7 visits, mostly in early pregnancy

question: A 30-year-old gravida 2 lady came to the clinic during her 38th week of gestation with complaints of labor pain. She had a dichorionic diamniotic, uncomplicated pregnancy. Her 1st twin was cephalic and was delivered vaginally. She is currently having uterine contractions every 5 minutes. On examination, her cervical os is 5 cm and the fetal heart rate is 150-160 beats per minute. Which of the following will be the next step in her management

answers.option: Artificial rupture of membranes and wait for spontaneous delivery
No need to intervene after delivery of first twin, do assessment of second twin

question: A 30-year-old gravida 4 para 3 lady is admitted to the labor ward for induction of labor at 40 weeks + 5 days of gestation. All her previous pregnancies ended with normal vaginal deliveries at term. She is induced with Prostaglandin E2. Which of the following could be the most likely complication?

A 30-year-old para 1+0 lady presents to the clinic after missing her period and with a positive urinary pregnancy test. Her previous baby has a congenital heart disease. Currently, she is eager to know about the fetal circulatory changes that occur at the time of birth. Which of the following should she be counseled about?

answers.option: Ductus arterioles remains open for a few days after birth
Rise in pressure in the right atrium

question: A 30-year-old gravida 3 para 2+0 lady is a known case of Hepatitis B. How can vertical transmission to her neonate be prevented?

answers.option: No measure can prevent vertical transmission
By giving immunoglobulins and Hepatitis B vaccine to neonate
Delivery by lower segment cesarean section

question: A 30-year-old para 2+0 lady with a body mass index of 35 kg/m² had an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) done during her 24th week of gestation to exclude gestational diabetes. Which one of the following is the correct WHO criteria for diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)?

A 30-year-old lady presents to the clinic on her 7th post-partum day complaining of pain and discomfort in perineal stitches. On examination, her episiotomy is partially open with foul-smelling lochia, redness, and swelling around the stitch line. She is also complaining of constipation for 4 days. Which of the following will be an appropriate first-line management for her?

answers.option: Send high vaginal swab for culture

question: A 30-year-old primigravida lady comes to the clinic for her antenatal checkup with an ultrasound scan showing 28 weeks of pregnancy with breech presentation. She is concerned about this and wants to know about the incidence of breech at term. Which of the following is correct about the incidence of breech presentation at term?

A 30-year-old para 5+3 lady presents to the antenatal clinic of a public sector hospital. She had her last baby 9 months ago. She now complains of lethargy and dyspnea. Her blood report shows a Hb of 6.6 gm/dl, MCV of 25 fl, MCH of 20 pg, and MCHC of 28 gm/dl. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her symptoms?

A 30-year-old gravida 2 para 1+0 lady came to the emergency department with signs and symptoms consistent with a thyroid goiter. She is a known case of Grave's disease and has been taking medications for it. Which of the following will be the drug of choice for this patient?
A 25-year-old gravida 2 para 1+0 is admitted with threatened preterm labor at 32 weeks of her pregnancy. Which of the following is the best treatment for her?

A 30-year-old gravida 2 lady came to the antenatal clinic for a routine checkup during her 28th week of gestation. Her blood pressure was 140/90 mmHg. Precise demonstration of diastolic blood pressure is a critical step in the diagnosis. Which Korotkoff sound is taken as a standard practice in measurement of diastolic blood pressure in pregnancy?

A 32-year-old primigravida was referred from a hospital in Badin with gestational amenorrhea for 35 weeks along with a history of fits. She had 2 episodes of fits in Badin and a further 2 episodes on her way to Karachi. On examination, her blood pressure (BP) was 170/120 mmHg, her pulse was 101 beats per minute, her temperature was 98.6 °F (37 °C) and her GCS was 12/15. On per abdominal examination, her height of fundus was 32 weeks with a cephalic presentation. Fetal heart sounds were audible and regular. Investigations showed urine albumin +++, Hb 8.9 g/dl, platelet count 150,000/cm, hematocrit 35, urea 70, creatinine 1.1, and a urine output of 100 cc. Which of the following will be the appropriate management in her case?

answers.option: Controlling BP, controlling fits with MgSO4 and termination of pregnancy
Controlling BP and starting maternal and fetal surveillance
Controlling BP and termination of pregnancy

question: A 32-year-old gravida 3 lady was admitted to the labor room in active labor with breech presentation. On examination, the estimated fetal weight was 3 kg (2.2 lb) and was noted to be an extended breech. An hour later, she was fully dilated and was pushing actively. After delivery of the buttocks and legs, the arms were found to be extended. Which of the following is the best method to deliver the baby's arms in this patient?

A 32-year-old para 1+0 woman has severe postpartum hemorrhage due to placenta previa that is not responding to therapy. The obstetrician says that surgical management is now needed. The patient plans on bearing children in the future. Which of the following is most appropriate and effective to achieve therapeutic goals in this patient?

A 32-year-old gravida 2 para 1+0 lady came to the antenatal clinic at 33 weeks of gestation with complaints of raised blood pressure for 15 days. Her lab reports show Hb as 9.6 g/dl, total leukocyte count as 5,800, platelets as 42,000, SGPT as 142 IU/L, LDH as 895 IU/L, urea as 18 mg/dl and creatinine as 0.6 mg/dl. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 32-year-old para 1+0 comes to the clinic with complaints of high-grade fever and breast tenderness for 3 days. She had a lower segment cesarean section done 7 days ago. On examination, her right breast appears engorged, red, edematous, and tender. Which of the following is the most common infective organism involved in this situation?
A 33-year-old para 2+0 obese lady with a BMI of 36 kg/m2 underwent an elective lower segment cesarean section at term. Which of the following is the most important postnatal care regarding her risks?

answers.option: Early mobilisation and avoidance of dehydration

question: A 34-year-old para 8+3 came to the antenatal clinic during her 16th week of gestation with complaints of breathlessness, lethargy, and palpitation. On examination, she is pale and her blood CP report shows low hemoglobin and a microcytic hypochromic peripheral smear. Which of the following will be the best test to reach the diagnosis?

A 34-year-old gravida 2 para 1+0 female presents at 37 weeks of gestation with absent fetal movements for one day. She has blood group O negative and has a previous history of baby born by vaginal delivery. She has a BMI of 32 kg/m^2 and a blood pressure of 140/90 mmHg. Ultrasound confirms intrauterine fetal demise and estimated fetal weight of 4.5 kg (9.9 lb) with polyhydramnios. Which of the following is the most probable cause of fetal demise?

A 35-year-old gravida 3 para 2+0 is admitted to the labor ward for her delivery in her 38th gestational week. She is HIV positive. Her symphysis fundal height is 35 cm. She is having regular contractions of 15-20 seconds every 3 minutes. Her cervix is 6 cm dilated and membranes are intact so far. Which of the following is an appropriate method to assess fetal compromise?

answers.option: Intermittent auscultation by hand-held doppler machine
Electronic monitoring of fetal heart rate

question: A 35-year-old diabetic woman delivers a preterm baby at 32 weeks of gestation. The patient gives a history of prolonged leaking prior to delivery. The baby develops respiratory distress syndrome (RDS). Which of the following factors is responsible for increased risk of RDS?

A 35-year-old primigravida comes to the clinic at 6 weeks of gestation. She is a known case of epilepsy and is on lamotrigine therapy with no history of fits for the past 8 months. Which of the following is the best advice for her?

answers.option: Prescribe methylcobalamin once per day in 1st trimester
Add a second drug also as she is at risk of developing fits during her pregnancy
Advise folic acid 5 mg per day in 1st trimester
Stop treatment as there is no history of fits since the last 8 months

question: A 35-year-old gravida 8 para 6+1 lady is brought to the emergency department in a collapsed state. She had a home delivery 5 hours ago by a midwife followed by heavy vaginal bleeding. Her blood pressure and pulse are un-recordable. The patient was resuscitated but she could not be revived. Which of the following could be the most probable cause of maternal death in her case?

A 36-year-old primigravida came to the clinic at 36 weeks of gestation. She is a known case of gestational diabetes. She wants to know her expected delivery date. Which of the following will be the best time for her to deliver?

A 36-year-old para 8+0 lady comes to the emergency department with a history of vaginal delivery of a healthy fetus 2 hours ago at home. She has been bleeding per vaginally since her delivery. On examination, her blood pressure is 90/60 mmHg and she is pale. On abdominal examination, her uterus felt soft and boggy. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her condition?

A 24-year-old primigravida lady comes to the emergency department during her 38th week of gestation complaining of liquor drainage for 3 hours. On examination, her blood pressure is 160/100 mmHg and her pulse is 80 beats per minute. On vaginal examination, the cervix is full length, displaced posteriorly and os is at 2 cm. Which of the following is the most appropriate method of induction of labor for her?

A 38-year-old gravida 3 para 2+0 lady comes to the emergency department during her 38th week of gestation with complaints of vaginal bleeding for 2 hours. She also complains of continuous abdominal pain. On examination, her blood pressure is 150/110 mmHg, her abdomen is tense and the fetal heart rate is 160 beats per minute. Which of the following will be the most appropriate management for her?

answers.option: Plan for immediate delivery after stabilisation
Ultrasound to rule out placental abruption

question: A 40-year-old gravida 1 para 0+0 lady comes during her 10th gestational week for screening for Down's syndrome. Which of the following is the best screening test recommended for Down's syndrome in the first trimester?

A grand multigravida presents to the antenatal clinic at 35 weeks of gestation. This is her first visit and she is complaining of breathlessness and extreme lethargy. Blood CP report shows Hb as 6 g/dl, MCV, MCH, MCHC, and serum ferritin levels are all decreased. Which of the following will be the first step in her management

A 25-year-old primigravida lady presented to the emergency department with a history of fits. She received intravenous magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) to control her fits. During her examination, she starts seizing again. Which of the following would be a drug of choice for this patient?
Which of the following is breast milk deficient in?
Safe motherhood is the concept or initiative to ensure high-quality maternal health. How many phases of delay can affect the quality of care offered to a mother?

A 35-year-old primigravida lady presented to the antenatal clinic for booking due to amenorrhea. She was found to be 18 weeks pregnant based on her last menstrual period. Her dating and anomaly scans are both normal. The patient has a family history of diabetes and her random blood sugar was found to be 120 mg/dl. Which of the following is the most relevant investigation for her?

answers.option: Oral glucose challenge test (OGCT) at 24 weeks
Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) at 24 weeks

question: A woman delivered a healthy baby girl 10 hours ago. Both mother and baby are doing well and the mother is feeling excited and is unable to sleep. Which of the following psychological change is she suffering from?

A 33-year-old gravida 3 para 2+0 woman was admitted to the labor room during her 38th gestational week with complaints of labor pains for over 6 hours. Which of the following is the correct presenting diameter of the fetal skull in a well-flexed head

A para 2+0 lady comes to the emergency room with complaints of painless vaginal bleeding for 3 hours. She has a previous history of 2 cesarean deliveries. She is currently 32 weeks pregnant. On examination, her blood pressure is 80/60 mmHg, her pulse is 120 beats per minute and the fetal heart rate is not detected on CTG. Which of the following is the most important step in the management of this patient

answers.option: Send for all baseline investigations and arrange blood
Counselling the family regarding the circumstances

question: A 32-year-old lady was admitted to the labor room for delivery at 35 weeks of gestation while she was 7 cm dilated. After 30 minutes, she had a spontaneous rupture of membranes with moderate vaginal bleeding. CTG revealed severe bradycardia. Which of the following is the most possible reason for this change?

A 25-year-old lady came to the antenatal clinic during her 34th gestational week. She had a symphysis fundal height of 26-28 cm. Her dating scan done at 14 weeks corresponds with her last menstrual period. Her Umbilical artery doppler examination shows absent diastolic velocity. Which of the following is an appropriate investigation that should now be performed on her?
Which of the following is the most common cause of maternal mortality worldwide?
Which of the following correctly describes the anatomy of the true pelvis in females?

answers.option: It is completely formed by 2 fused bones
It has 3 defining planes; an inlet, a mid-cavity and an outlet
It has an inlet made of a double triangle
It lies between the wings of a paired ileum

question: In the year 2000 at the UN millennium summit, the UN millennium declaration was signed which had some goals that were to be achieved by the year 2015. How many goals were included in the UN millennium developmental goals (MDGs)?

An 18-year-old girl was admitted to the labor room with regular contractions. She had a prolonged second stage of labor due to which forceps had to be used. Her baby died 24 hours after delivery due to birth asphyxia. She is now very anxious and tearful about the outcome of her pregnancy. Which of the following is an appropriate treatment option for her?

A 34-year-old gravida 5 para 4+0 lady came to the antenatal clinic with reduced fetal movements. She was unbooked and her last menstrual period was more than 9 months ago, but she does not remember the exact date. On examination, her symphysis-fundal height was 40 cm, and presenting part was breech. Which of the following is the most common cause of post-term pregnancy?

A young primigravida came to the antenatal clinic during her 34th gestational week. On examination, her symphysis fundal height is 30 cm. Ultrasound revealed an alive fetus with a disparity in biometry and reduced liquor. Biparietal diameter is normal but abdominal circumference is reduced. Which of the following is the most probable cause?

A primigravida came to the labor room at 39 weeks of gestation. In her first stage of labor, while she was 6 cm dilated, a CTG was performed which showed a baseline fetal heart rate of 140 beats per minute and one deceleration associated with contractions. What is the significance of this deceleration?

answers.option: Very significant if associated with 5-10 beats variability
Very significant if associated with tachycardia

question: A primigravida presented at 38 weeks of gestation with breech presentation. Her blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg and there is +2 proteinuria. Her symphysis fundal height measures 32 cm. Which of the following is the best management option for this patient?

A 24-year-old lady comes to the antenatal clinic with a positive urine pregnancy test which she did after missing a period. Which wants to know the best time to perform a dating scan. Which of the following is an appropriate time for this scan?
A primigravida at 26 weeks of gestation is advised for cordocentesis. Which of the following is the most common reason for performing cordocentesis?

A 26-year-old primigravida delivered her baby via forceps. A midline episiotomy had to be done during her delivery which got extended. Which of the following is a disadvantage of performing a midline episiotomy?

answers.option: Risk of extension till anal sphincter

question: A para 8+0 lady delivered a 4 kg (8.8 lb) baby at home after prolonged labor. She was brought to the hospital in a collapsed state. Her abdomen is distended, tense, and tender. There is a trickle of bright red blood coming from her vagina. Which of the following is an appropriate cause of her condition?

A 25-year-old primigravida has come into the outpatient department complaining of persistently high blood pressure for the past month. On examination, her blood pressure is 140/95 mmHg, she is edematous, and her symphysio-fundal height is 32 cm. The fetal presentation is cephalic and the fetal heart sounds are 142 bpm. Which of the following investigations should be performed first for this patient?

A 26-year-old woman, para 2+0, who is a known case of mitral stenosis has presented with complaints of dyspnea while doing routine work. Her current gestational age is 34 weeks. Accordingly, which of the following New York Heart Association (NYHA) classes are appropriate for this patient?
